clues.clue: This kind of AI system is a language model that can call tools in a loop until it finishes a task.
clues.quote: An AI agent is a language model that can call tools in a loop until it finishes a task.

clues.clue: A tool is described by a name, a description, and one of these for its arguments.
clues.quote: described by a name, a description, and a JSON schema for its arguments

clues.clue: The model never runs a tool itself; this does, which is where permissions and logging belong.
clues.quote: The model never runs the tool itself; the surrounding code does, which is where permissions and logging belong.

clues.clue: Forcing a model to return data that fits a schema, like a Pydantic model, is called this.
clues.quote: Structured output means the model must return data that fits a schema, such as a Pydantic model.

clues.clue: Structured output lets code check the answer this way instead of parsing free text.
clues.quote: This lets code check the answer field by field instead of parsing free text.

clues.clue: This open standard, abbreviated MCP, lets an agent discover and call tools exposed by a server.
clues.quote: The Model Context Protocol, or MCP, is an open standard that lets an agent discover and call tools exposed by a server.

clues.clue: A local MCP server communicates over this channel.
clues.quote: An MCP server can run locally over stdio or remotely over HTTP.

clues.clue: A remote MCP server communicates over this protocol.
clues.quote: An MCP server can run locally over stdio or remotely over HTTP.

clues.clue: With the database behind an MCP server, agents can only touch data through these.
clues.quote: agents can only touch data through the tools the server chooses to expose

clues.clue: A good MCP tool returns only what is in the data and never does this to values.
clues.quote: A good MCP tool returns only what is actually in the data and never invents values.

clues.clue: Providers bill by the number of input and output these.
clues.quote: providers bill by the number of input and output tokens

clues.clue: Roughly, one token is about this many characters of English.
clues.quote: roughly three to four characters of English

clues.clue: These tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens.
clues.quote: Output tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens.

clues.clue: Cached input tokens are often billed at this fraction of the normal input price.
clues.quote: often one tenth of the normal input price

clues.clue: To benefit from caching, long static content goes here in the prompt.
clues.quote: put the long static content, such as instructions and a handbook, at the start of the prompt

clues.clue: This attack hides instructions inside data so that a model treats them as commands.
clues.quote: Prompt injection is an attack that hides instructions inside data so that a model treats them as commands.

clues.clue: Text of this color in a PDF is a classic place to hide an injection.
clues.quote: Examples include white text in a PDF

clues.clue: In layered defense, this layer removes hidden text before any model sees it.
clues.quote: The code layer removes hidden text before any model sees it

clues.clue: Requiring every reported fact to be traceable to the source is called this.
clues.quote: Grounding means every fact an agent reports must be traceable to the source.

clues.clue: Deliberately attacking your own system to find weaknesses before real users do.
clues.quote: Red teaming means deliberately attacking your own system to find weaknesses before real users do.

final.clue: In the safest design, agents may request money movements, but only these get the tool that actually moves the money.
final.quote: The safest design lets agents request money movements but gives only humans the tool that actually moves the money.
